title: System.exit() usage in the AeroTopo project
answer: For this AeroTopo codebase, the accurate project answer is that `System.exit()` is not used in the normal Spring Boot service code. The application starts with `SpringApplication.run`, and deployment/rollback is handled by the runtime and deployment environment rather than by business code terminating the JVM. I would avoid `System.exit()` in controllers, services, and reusable libraries because one call can terminate the entire process. I would reserve an explicit exit status for a standalone command-line or one-shot tool where ending the process is intentionally part of the program contract.

steps.why_te: AeroTopo main method SpringApplication ni start chestundi; direct `System.exit` ledu. Long-running service lifecycle ni framework and deployment environment manage chestayi. Business request code whole JVM ni stop cheyyakudadhu.

steps.question: The highlighted runbook line treats startup, verification, traffic switching, and rollback as controlled operational steps. steps.why_te: Highlighted deployment line controlled rollout and rollback ni show chestundi. Controller/service direct exit chesthe whole process sudden ga stop avvachu. Exceptions and framework lifecycle handling service context lo safer.
